newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO urges U.N. action against Israel over settlement.
newsitem.headline: PLO urges U.N. action against Israel over settlement.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation called on the General Assembly on Tuesday to take action against Israel for refusing to halt construction of a settlement in territory south of Jerusalem captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

A resolution submitted to a resumed emergency special session of the Assembly would request that U.N. members halt any support, by companies and individuals, for Israeli settlements in occupied territories and to bar any imports produced in the settlements.

The draft would condemn Israel's failure to comply with a resolution adopted in April by a vote of 134-3, with 11 abstentions, demanding a halt to the construction of 6,500 homes at a site called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic, as well as other settlement activities.

A recent report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan criticising Israel's continued building at Har Homa/Jabal Abu Ghneim and elsewhere in the occupied terrritories prompted the Arab group of states to call for a resumption of the special session.

The PLO's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, told the Assembly: "The illegal Israeli actions must be stopped. The building of the settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim must be stopped. Colonial settlement, in all its aspects, must be stopped. The attempts to Judaize and seize Jerusalem must be stopped ... because they grossly violate international law and legitimacy, as well as the agreements reached between the parties."
The "whole world is unanimous in rejecting Israeli practices related to settlements and to Jerusalem," he added.

Al-Kidwa said the Palestinian people and their leadership were still committed to their "strategic decision to engage in the peace process and to uphold the agreements reached. We still have not completely lost hope for a qualitative change in the Israeli position necessary to salvage the peace process and bring it back on track."

He said the Palestinian people had the "unshaken, deep conviction that our people will be able to regain all of their inalienable rights and will be able to establish their independent state with Jerusalem as its capital."

Israel's newly appointed U.N. ambassador, Dore Gold, formerly a political adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said: "While Israel has met all of its commitments, the PLO has met none of its obligations."

Israel had completed its redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, released convicted "terrorists" from prison, transferred large funds to the Palestinian Authority and was ready to resume negotiations on all outstanding interim issues and to restart negotiations on so-called final status issues.

But Gold said the PLO had failed to revise the Palestinian National Covenant calling for Israel's destruction, repeatedly cut off security cooperation with Israel, failed to end incitement to violence, released "Hamas and Islamic Jihad terrorists" from jail, failed to confiscate illegal arms and failed to reduce the number of Palestinian police to the agreed level.

"Let no member of this assembly delude themselves that this session will, in any way, advance prospects for peace in our region," said Gold in his maiden U.N. speech. He has not yet presented his credentials as ambassador and was speaking as a special envoy.
More than 30 other speakers, mostly from Arab and Moslem countries, were scheduled to take part in the debate.
